newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan calls for calm in islands dispute.
newsitem.headline: Japan calls for calm in islands dispute.

text.p: Japan, its foreign policy on hold because of a looming general election, sought on Tuesday to calm passions in a dispute over islands claimed by it, China and Taiwan.

In a bid to cool tempers, Japan has asked China and Taiwan to prevent a recurrence of Monday's "illegal landings" on the disputed islands in the East China Sea, a Foreign Ministry official told Reuters on Tuesday.

The official declined to say what steps Japan would take if activists from Taiwan, Hong Kong and elsewhere tried again to enter what it said were Japan's territorial waters and set foot on the islands.
"What we really want the countries concerned to do is to calm down," he said.

On Monday, some 300 Taiwanese and Hong Kong protesters aboard a 50-boat flotilla pierced a Japanese maritime cordon around the islands and briefly raised the flags of Beijing and Taipei on the rocky outcrops in a challenge to Tokyo's claim of sovereignty.

Last Friday, Japan had announced it would not recognise a lighthouse built on one of the islands by a Japanese right-wing group. The building of the lighthouse rekindled the dispute over the islands, known as the Senkakus in Japanese and the Diaoyus in Chinese.
Rivals China and Taiwan, which separately challenge Japan's claim to the uninhabited islands, condemned the construction of the lighthouse and demanded its immediate removal.
Japan's claim dates to 1895, when it defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. Tokyo says the issue is not open for discussion.
China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
Taiwan has no diplomatic ties with Japan, which only recognises Beijing's Communist government.
"We think that it is very important that the situation should calm down," Foreign Ministry spokesman Hiroshi Hashimoto told a regular news conference on Tuesday.
"Both China and Japan share the same view that this matter shouldn't jeopardise the bilateral relationship between Japan and China," he added.

Diplomatic sources said with Japan holding general elections on October 20, there was unlikely to be any major breakthrough on the dispute until after that date, when new policy positions could be discussed.
Japan is also involved in separate territorial disputes with South Korea and Russia and has so far been equally determined not to give ground in these disputes.
In each case, the waters around the islands concerned are rich in fisheries and are thought to contain oil.
